key_insight: Classical polynomial-time algorithms can estimate local thermal observables in SYK and related mean-field models at all constant temperatures, extending up to the glass transition.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the assumed need for quantum resources in thermal-state analysis and provides a rigorous pathway for scalable inference and learning from Gibbs states in strongly interacting systems.
method: Develop a fully rigorous quantum cavity method.
Extend the analysis from SYK to classical spin-glass models.
Use the Gibbs state to learn SYK Hamiltonians with polynomial time and sample complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees rather than empirical benchmarks, with results on constant-temperature local observables and a learning algorithm with polynomial time and sample complexity.
watch_item: The guarantees are for constant temperatures and local observables, so broader finite-size behavior and practical implementation costs may differ.
paper_title: Polynomial-time classical algorithms for mean-field models up to the glass transition
